stem.text: Sand is delivered to a building site at a rate of P(t) tons per hour, where P is differentiable and t is measured in hours. Measured values are P(0) = 5, P(4) = 9, P(8) = 12, P(12) = 7. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{12} P(t)\,dt \), the number of tons of sand delivered from t = 0 to t = 12, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 4 \cdot \frac{5 + 9}{2} = 28 \); \( 4 \cdot \frac{9 + 12}{2} = 42 \); \( 4 \cdot \frac{12 + 7}{2} = 38 \).

distractor_derivations.B: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.C: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
distractor_derivations.D: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
